stimulus: An agronomist measured the grain yield, in bushels per acre, of 10 test plots of a new wheat variety, and the mean yield was 62 bushels per acre. Two more plots were then harvested, and each had the same yield, $x$ bushels per acre. The mean yield of all 12 plots was 65 bushels per acre.
explanation: Turn each mean into a total. The 10 plots total $10 \times 62 = 620$ bushels per acre, and all 12 plots total $12 \times 65 = 780$. So the two new plots add up to $780 - 620 = 160$. They have equal yields, so $x = 160 \div 2 = 80$.

A.why: You multiplied the new mean by the old count of 10 instead of the new count of 12. That gives $650 - 620 = 30$ for the two plots, and then $15$ each. Once the two new values are added, the count is 12.

B.why: You set $\frac{62 + x}{2} = 65$, which averages the old mean with the new value as if both groups were the same size. The original group has 10 plots and the new group has only 2, so you have to work with totals.

D.why: 160 is the combined yield of the two new plots. You stopped before dividing by 2 to find the yield of each plot.

stem: What is the range of the seven weekly counts?
stimulus: A county health department recorded the number of new influenza cases reported each week for seven weeks. In increasing order, the counts were $3$, $6$, $9$, $x$, $14$, $17$, and $y$. The median of the seven counts is 11, and the mean is 12.
explanation: There are seven values in order, so the median is the 4th one, which means $x = 11$. A mean of 12 means the counts total $7 \times 12 = 84$. The known values add to $3 + 6 + 9 + 11 + 14 + 17 = 60$, so $y = 24$. The range is $24 - 3 = 21$.

A.why: You used a count of 6 instead of 7 when you found the total ($6 \times 12 = 72$). That gives $y = 12$, which is less than 17 and breaks the increasing order. You left the unknown out of the count.

B.why: You found $y - x = 24 - 11$. The range is the maximum minus the minimum, and the minimum is 3, not $x$.

C.why: You used the mean, 12, as the middle value. That gives $x = 12$ and $y = 23$. The median is 11, so $x = 11$.

stimulus: Two seismic stations recorded the focal depths, in kilometers, of the earthquakes each detected in one month. Station P recorded five earthquakes with depths of 12, 18, 25, 9, and $x$ kilometers. Station Q recorded four earthquakes with depths of 14, 20, 11, and 23 kilometers. The mean depth at Station P was 2 kilometers greater than the mean depth at Station Q.
explanation: Station Q's mean depth is $\frac{14 + 20 + 11 + 23}{4} = \frac{68}{4} = 17$ km, so Station P's mean is $17 + 2 = 19$ km. Station P's five depths must total $5 \times 19 = 95$. The four known depths add to 64, so $x = 95 - 64 = 31$.

A.why: You made Station P's mean 2 km smaller than Station Q's ($17 - 2 = 15$), which gives a total of 75. The text says Station P's mean is greater.

B.why: You multiplied 19 by 4 instead of 5 and got 76. Station P has five depths once you count $x$, so the total is $5 \times 19 = 95$.

C.why: 19 km is the mean depth Station P needs. The question asks for the missing depth $x$, which you find from the total.

stem: How many map sheets did Surveyor B digitize?
stimulus: Two surveyors at a mapping agency digitized paper map sheets. Surveyor A digitized 18 sheets in a mean time of 40 minutes per sheet. Surveyor B digitized some sheets in a mean time of 50 minutes per sheet. The mean time for all sheets digitized by both surveyors was 44 minutes per sheet.
explanation: Let $n$ be the number of sheets Surveyor B digitized. Adding the totals gives $18(40) + 50n = 44(18 + n)$, which is $720 + 50n = 792 + 44n$. So $6n = 72$ and $n = 12$. You can check: $\frac{720 + 600}{30} = 44$.

B.why: You assumed both surveyors digitized the same number of sheets. If they had, the combined mean would be the plain average of 40 and 50, which is 45. The combined mean is 44, which is closer to 40, so Surveyor B must have digitized fewer sheets.

C.why: 30 is the combined number of sheets, $18 + 12$. The question asks only for the number Surveyor B digitized.

D.why: 72 is the value of $6n$. You stopped before dividing by 6.

stimulus: An ecologist counted the nesting pairs of a seabird on six islands. The counts were 14, 9, 22, 17, 11, and $x$, where $x$ is a whole number. The median of the six counts is 15.5, the range is greater than 13, and the mean is an integer less than 17.
explanation: In order, the known counts are 9, 11, 14, 17, 22. A median of 15.5 is the average of 14 and 17, so $x \geq 17$. If $x \leq 22$, the range is $22 - 9 = 13$, which is not greater than 13, so $x > 22$. For the mean to be an integer, $73 + x$ must be a multiple of 6, so $x$ could be 23, 29, and so on. Only $x = 23$ gives a mean less than 17: $\frac{96}{6} = 16$.

A.why: 16 is the mean of the six counts when $x = 23$. The question asks for $x$.

B.why: 17 meets the median condition and gives an integer mean of 15. But the range would then be $22 - 9 = 13$, and the range has to be greater than 13. You stopped before checking every condition.

D.why: 29 meets the median and range conditions, and the mean is an integer. But the mean is $\frac{102}{6} = 17$, and it has to be less than 17. You stopped before checking every condition.

stem: What is the titer of the other removed sample?
stimulus: An immunology lab measured the antibody titers of 8 serum samples, and the mean titer was 45 units. Two samples were later found to be contaminated and were removed. The mean titer of the remaining 6 samples was 43 units. One of the removed samples had a titer of 50 units.
explanation: The 8 samples total $8 \times 45 = 360$ units, and the 6 remaining samples total $6 \times 43 = 258$. The two removed samples therefore add up to $360 - 258 = 102$. One of them is 50, so the other is $102 - 50 = 52$.

A.why: 51 is the mean of the two removed samples, $102 \div 2$. You need the second sample's own titer, which is $102 - 50$.

C.why: You multiplied by 7 instead of 6 ($7 \times 43 = 301$), as if only one sample had been removed, and got $360 - 301 = 59$. Two samples were removed, so 6 remain.

D.why: 102 is the combined titer of both removed samples. You still need to subtract the known 50.

stimulus: A labor economist studied the hourly wages at a warehouse. The 30 part-time workers earned a mean hourly wage of $\$18.00$. The 20 full-time workers earned a mean hourly wage of $\$x$. The mean hourly wage of all 50 workers was $\$21.60$.
explanation: All 50 workers earn a total of $50 \times 21.60 = \$1{,}080$ per hour, and the part-time workers earn $30 \times 18 = \$540$. That leaves $\$540$ for the 20 full-time workers, so $x = \frac{540}{20} = 27.00$.

A.why: You divided the full-time workers' $\$540$ by all 50 workers instead of by the 20 full-time workers.

B.why: You set $\frac{18 + x}{2} = 21.60$, which averages the two group means as if both groups had the same number of workers. There are 30 part-time workers and only 20 full-time workers, so you have to combine totals.

D.why: $\$540$ is the total hourly pay of the full-time workers. You stopped before dividing by 20 to get their mean.

stimulus: A linguist recorded the number of consonant sounds in seven languages. In increasing order, the counts were $a$, $22$, $28$, $b$, $36$, $41$, and $a + 30$. The median of the seven counts is 31, and the mean is 32.
explanation: With seven values in order, the median is the 4th value, so $b = 31$. A mean of 32 means the counts total $7 \times 32 = 224$. The sum is $a + 22 + 28 + 31 + 36 + 41 + (a + 30) = 2a + 188$. Setting $2a + 188 = 224$ gives $2a = 36$, so $a = 18$. The ordered list is 18, 22, 28, 31, 36, 41, 48.

A.why: You multiplied the mean by 6 instead of 7, which gives $2a + 188 = 192$. That makes the largest count $a + 30 = 32$, which is less than 36 and breaks the increasing order. All seven values, including both expressions in $a$, count toward the total.

C.why: 36 is the value of $2a$. You stopped before dividing by 2.

D.why: 48 is the largest count, $a + 30$. The question asks for $a$, the smallest count.
